name: Mesquite
seo_title: Mesquite, TX Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 5 Events
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Mesquite, TX: Christmas on the Square, Christmas in the Park at Westlake Park, Christmas at the Ranch and A Christmas Story.
lede: The story of Christmas in Mesquite starts in 1873, when the Texas and Pacific Railway made Mesquite a depot town, and runs through a tree lighting at Heritage Square, a two day Christmas in the Park and an open house at the Florence Ranch Homestead, a farmhouse built in 1871 and 1872. Mesquite packs its holiday into early December, with Santa, fireworks and a free homestead morning.
sections: Christmas on the Square and Christmas in the Park

Mesquite lights its downtown tree at Heritage Square, 111 S Broad Street, on Tuesday, December 1, 2026. Grounds open at 5 pm, the mayor starts the ceremony at 6 pm, a local choir sings 12 Days of Downtown Mesquite and student representatives help light the tree. Santa visits, free cocoa and cookies go out while they last, and a gift market runs alongside. Then Christmas in the Park fills Westlake Park, 600 Gross Road, on December 5 and 6 from 2 to 8 pm. Entry and parking are free, activity wristbands cost $12 for residents and $15 for non-residents, and each evening ends with a Santa sendoff and fireworks.

Historic Mesquite, Inc. opens the Florence Ranch Homestead, 1424 Barnes Bridge Road, on Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 10 am to 1 pm for crafts and treats. The host's own Facebook post says it is a free event open to everyone. The farmhouse was built in 1871 and 1872 by David W. and Julia Florence, and the city celebrated 150 years of the homestead with a Christmas open house in December 2021. Kids get a look at an old Texas farmhouse dressed for the season.
A depot town on the Texas and Pacific

Mesquite's story is a railroad story. The Handbook of Texas says the Texas and Pacific Railway established the town as a depot in May 1873, bypassing the older community of Scyene, and that the name comes from nearby Mesquite Creek. Growth came much later: the town had 1,696 people in 1950 and 27,526 in 1960. The Mesquite Championship Rodeo began its continuous run in 1958, and Town East Mall opened in 1971. DART opened its 4.5 mile Blue Line extension from Downtown Garland Station to Downtown Rowlett Station on December 3, 2012.

faq: The Handbook of Texas says the Texas and Pacific Railway established Mesquite as a depot in May 1873, bypassing the older community of Scyene. The railroad is the reason the town exists, and downtown grew up around the depot while the older settlement faded.
How did Mesquite get its name?

According to the Handbook of Texas, the name comes from nearby Mesquite Creek. The Texas and Pacific Railway chose the creek's name for its new depot in 1873, and the town has carried it ever since, from a depot stop to a city with a rodeo, a mall and a light rail line.
What happens at Christmas for kids in Mesquite?

Heritage Square lights its tree on Tuesday, December 1, 2026, with Santa, free cocoa and cookies. Christmas in the Park fills Westlake Park on December 5 and 6 from 2 to 8 pm, with Santa and fireworks each evening. Entry is free, and activity wristbands cost $12 for residents and $15 for non residents.
Is there a free Christmas event at a historic site in Mesquite?

Yes. Historic Mesquite, Inc. opens the Florence Ranch Homestead, 1424 Barnes Bridge Road, on Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 10 am to 1 pm for crafts and treats. The host's own Facebook post says it is free and open to everyone. The farmhouse was built in 1871 and 1872.
Who organizes Christmas events in Mesquite?

The City of Mesquite lists Christmas on the Square and Christmas in the Park, with downtown partners behind the tree lighting. Historic Mesquite, Inc. hosts Christmas at the Ranch, and Mesquite Arts Theatre stages A Christmas Story on weekends from November 27 to December 13, 2026.
Can you take light rail to Mesquite or nearby Christmas events?

DART opened its 4.5 mile Blue Line extension from Downtown Garland Station to Downtown Rowlett Station on December 3, 2012. Garland and Rowlett are both neighbors of Mesquite, so families can combine a light rail ride with the Garland and Rowlett Christmas events listed on their own Rally pages.
